terms.def: A radio that combines a transmitter and a receiver in one unit.
terms.more: A mobile transceiver is one made to be used in a vehicle. A multimode transceiver can work in several modes, such as FM, SSB and CW.

terms.def: Equipment that provides the DC voltage and current a radio needs to run.
terms.more: It is rated in volts and amperes. A typical 50-watt mobile FM transceiver needs 13.8 volts at 12 amperes, because the radio draws much more power than it sends out.

terms.def: The unit of voltage, the electrical push that makes current flow.
terms.more: Mobile radios are built for a vehicle's 12-volt electrical system, so a suitable power supply is rated 13.8 volts.

terms.def: The unit of electric current, the amount of electricity flowing.
terms.more: A power supply must be able to deliver enough amperes for the radio. A typical 50-watt mobile FM transceiver needs a 12-ampere supply.

terms.def: The unit of power, the rate at which energy is used or sent out.
terms.more: Volts times amperes gives watts. A transmitter takes more watts from its supply than it sends out as RF, because some is lost as heat.

terms.def: Frequency modulation: a way of sending voice by varying the frequency of the radio signal.
terms.more: It is the usual mode for handheld and mobile radios and repeaters. An FM signal received slightly off frequency sounds distorted.

terms.def: Standing wave ratio: a measure of how well the antenna system is matched to the feed line.
terms.more: It is read with an SWR meter placed in the feed line.

terms.def: An instrument that shows how well the antenna system is matched to the feed line.
terms.more: When choosing one, consider the frequency and power level at which the measurements will be made. It only measures the match; it cannot correct a poor one.

terms.def: How many times per second a radio wave repeats; it is the number you tune the radio to.
terms.more: The operating frequency of a transceiver can be entered with the keypad or the VFO knob. Test instruments such as SWR meters are built for a certain frequency range.

terms.def: Direct current: electricity that flows steadily in one direction, as from a battery or a radio power supply.
terms.more: A transceiver's DC power connection uses short, heavy-gauge wires.

terms.def: The voltage lost along a wire because the wire has resistance and current is flowing through it.
terms.more: A radio draws its highest current when transmitting. Short, heavy-gauge DC power wires keep the loss small.

terms.def: Thick wire, which has less resistance than thin wire of the same length.
terms.more: Short, heavy-gauge wires are used for a transceiver's DC power connection to minimize voltage drop when transmitting.

terms.def: A weak-signal digital mode in which computer software turns short messages into audio tones and decodes the tones that are received.
terms.more: The transceiver's audio input and output are connected to the audio output and input of a computer running FT8 software.

terms.def: A way of communicating in which a computer or digital radio sends information as data instead of plain analog voice.
terms.more: With a computer, the radio and computer trade audio: for example the transceiver's speaker connector goes to the computer's line in.

terms.def: The connections between a computer and a radio that let the computer operate digital modes through the radio.
terms.more: It carries three signals: receive audio, transmit audio, and transmitter keying.

terms.def: Switching a radio from receive to transmit.
terms.more: It is one of the three signals in a computer-radio interface for digital modes, along with receive audio and transmit audio.

terms.def: The audio input connector on a computer, where sound from another device is fed in.
terms.more: For digital modes the computer's line in connects to the transceiver's speaker connector, so the computer hears what the radio receives. Line out is the computer's audio output.

terms.def: The connector on a transceiver where received audio comes out for an external speaker or other device.
terms.more: It is an audio output, so for digital modes it connects to an audio input: the computer's line in.

terms.def: Radio frequency: the kind of electrical energy a transmitter makes and an antenna radiates as radio waves.
terms.more: RF power flows from the transmitter through the feed line to the antenna. RF current travels on the surface of a conductor.

terms.def: An instrument that measures the radio-frequency power a transmitter is sending toward the antenna.
terms.more: It is installed in the feed line, between the transmitter and the antenna.

terms.def: The cable that carries radio signals between a radio and its antenna.
terms.more: Meters that measure RF power are installed in the feed line, between the transmitter and the antenna.

terms.def: The part of a station that turns the transmitter's RF power into radio waves and picks up radio waves for the receiver.
terms.more: It is connected to the radio by the feed line.

terms.def: Connecting pieces of station equipment together with a conductor so that they all stay at the same voltage.
terms.more: Flat copper strap is the preferred conductor for bonding at RF.

terms.def: A wide, flat strip of copper used as a conductor.
terms.more: It is the preferred conductor for bonding at RF, because its large surface gives RF current an easy path.

terms.def: The unit of battery capacity: how much current a battery can deliver multiplied by how long it can deliver it.
terms.more: To find how long a battery can power equipment, divide its ampere-hour rating by the average current draw of the equipment.

terms.def: The amount of current, in amperes, that a piece of equipment takes from its battery or power supply.
terms.more: Battery run time is the ampere-hour rating divided by the average current draw, not the peak.

terms.def: A small, very low power device that links nearby digital transceivers to a digital voice or data network.
terms.more: Your radio talks to the hotspot over a short radio hop, and the hotspot usually reaches the network through the internet.

terms.def: Voice that the radio converts into digital data before sending it.
terms.more: DMR and D-STAR are digital voice systems. A hotspot can connect nearby transceivers to a digital voice network.

terms.def: The negative wire of a radio's DC power cable, which carries the current back to the battery.
terms.more: In a vehicle, connect it at the 12-volt battery chassis ground, not to just any metal part.

terms.def: The point where a vehicle's battery negative lead is fastened to the metal body of the vehicle.
terms.more: The negative power return of a mobile transceiver should be connected at the 12-volt battery chassis ground.

terms.def: A device that assists in manual sending of Morse code.
terms.more: It forms evenly timed dits and dahs while the operator works a pair of paddles.

terms.def: A code that spells out letters and numbers as patterns of short and long signals, called dits and dahs.
terms.more: An electronic keyer helps an operator send it by hand.

terms.def: The control that sets how strongly the sound from your microphone drives the transmitter.
terms.more: Excessive microphone gain on SSB causes distorted transmitted audio.

terms.def: Single sideband: a voice mode that sends only one of the two sidebands of an AM signal.
terms.more: A 2400 Hz receive filter suits SSB. If a received SSB voice sounds too high or low in pitch, adjust the RIT or clarifier.

terms.def: Variable frequency oscillator: the tuning control of a transceiver, which you turn to change the operating frequency.
terms.more: The operating frequency can be entered with the keypad or the VFO knob.

terms.def: A receiver control that mutes the speaker until a signal stronger than a set threshold arrives.
terms.more: To hear a weak FM signal, set the squelch threshold so that the receiver output audio is on all the time.

terms.def: Tuned a little above or below the frequency that the signal is actually on.
terms.more: An FM signal received slightly off frequency sounds distorted. On SSB, mistuning makes the voice pitch too high or too low instead.

terms.def: A transceiver function that tunes through a range of frequencies to check for activity.
terms.more: The radio steps through frequencies or memory channels by itself and stops when it hears a signal.

terms.def: Receiver incremental tuning: a control that shifts only the receive frequency slightly, leaving the transmit frequency where it is.
terms.more: Also called a clarifier. Use it when the voice pitch of an SSB signal seems too high or too low.

terms.def: A general call that invites any station to answer.
terms.more: If the voice of an SSB station answering your CQ sounds too high or low, adjust the RIT or clarifier instead of moving your transmit frequency.

terms.def: Digital Mobile Radio: a digital voice system in which many groups of users share the same repeaters.
terms.more: A DMR radio is set up by loading a code plug. A specific group of stations is selected by entering that group's identification code.

terms.def: The configuration data loaded onto a DMR radio so that it can access repeaters and talkgroups.
terms.more: It is a file of settings, not a physical plug or cable.

terms.def: A named or numbered group of stations on a DMR network that hear each other's transmissions.
terms.more: You select a specific group on a DMR transceiver by entering the group's identification code.

terms.def: A station that receives a signal and retransmits it at the same time, so that stations can reach farther.
terms.more: A DMR code plug holds the settings a radio needs to access repeaters and talkgroups.

terms.def: The width of the slice of frequencies that a receiver's filter lets through.
terms.more: Choosing a bandwidth that matches the mode reduces noise and interference. For SSB, 2400 Hz gives the best signal-to-noise ratio.

terms.def: The method used to put information on a radio signal, such as FM, SSB or CW.
terms.more: Each mode takes up a different width of spectrum, so a multimode transceiver offers a choice of receiver filter bandwidths.

terms.def: A comparison of how strong the wanted signal is with how strong the background noise is.
terms.more: A receive filter just wide enough for the signal gives the best ratio. For SSB that is 2400 Hz.

terms.def: The unit of frequency: one hertz is one cycle per second.
terms.more: Filter bandwidths are given in hertz. A 2400 Hz filter is the best fit for SSB reception.

terms.def: A digital voice system for amateur radio that sends data, including your identity, along with your voice.
terms.more: Your call sign must be programmed into a D-STAR transceiver before transmitting.

terms.def: The unique set of letters and numbers that the FCC assigns to identify a licensed station.
terms.more: It must be programmed into a D-STAR digital transceiver before transmitting.
